subQuestions.questionText: Aggie and 14 friends started a stokvel in order to buy groceries. The grocery items bought will be shared equally among all the members of the stokvel. TABLE 1 shows the comparison of prices, excluding VAT, of items she needs to buy at two wholesalers A and B. Canned fish quantity is 12 cans × 400 g, with 10 packs purchased. Write down how many cans of fish each member of the stokvel will receive.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Number of tins = $12 \times 10 = 120$ (multiplying by 10)
Mark 2: Number of tins each member gets = $120 \div 15$ (dividing by 15)
Mark 3: $= 8$ cans (simplification, AO)

subQuestions.questionText: Aggie stated that she could load all these items onto her half-ton bakkie without overloading it. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is valid. (Items: Cake flour 12,5 kg × 15; Maize meal 5 kg × 30; Rama 125 g × 48 in a packet × 15; Rice 10 kg × 15; Canned fish 12 cans × 400 g × 10; Long-life milk 6-pack of 1 ℓ × 15; Spice 10 × 50 g × 15. Note: 1 ℓ ≈ 1 kg)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $12,5 \text{ kg} \times 15 = 187,5 \text{ kg}$ (multiplying by quantity)
Mark 2: Conversion g to kg: $0,125 \text{ kg} \times 48 \times 15 = 90 \text{ kg}$
Mark 3: Adding all values
Mark 4: Conversion ℓ to kg: $6 \times 15 \text{ kg} = 90 \text{ kg}$

Full breakdown:
- Cake flour: $12,5 \times 15 = 187,5$ kg
- Maize meal: $5 \times 30 = 150$ kg
- Rama: $0,125 \times 48 \times 15 = 90$ kg
- Rice: $10 \times 15 = 150$ kg
- Canned fish: $12 \times 0,4 \times 10 = 48$ kg
- Long-life milk: $6 \times 15 = 90$ kg
- Spice: $10 \times 0,05 \times 15 = 7,5$ kg

Mark 5: Total = $723$ kg (simplification)
Mark 6: Half ton = $500$ kg (half ton value)
Mark 7: Conclusion: NOT VALID, the total mass (723 kg) is more than half a ton (500 kg), so it cannot fit into a half-ton bakkie.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine, showing ALL calculations, which wholesaler (A or B) will be cheaper if she buys all the items (including VAT) from one wholesaler.
subQuestions.memoText:
For Wholesaler A:
Mark 1: Total cost of items where VAT must be added = $R1\,274,85 + R689,70 + R4\,154,85 + R1\,499,85$ (adding items subject to VAT)
Mark 2: $= R7\,619,25$ (simplification)
Mark 3: VAT amount = $R7\,619,25 \times 15\% = R1\,142,89$ (multiplying by 15%)
Mark 4: Simplification of VAT amount
Mark 5: Total amount = $R7\,619,25 + R1\,142,89 + R1\,679,85 + R1\,559,50 + R1\,049,85$ (adding all values)
Mark 6: $= R13\,051,34$ (simplification)
Mark 7: Wholesaler A is cheaper (R13 051,34 < R13 102,40 of Wholesaler B). [Choose Wholesaler A]

subQuestions.questionText: The food inflation rate was 5,17% in January 2021 and is estimated to be 5,3% in January 2022. Calculate the total amount for 5 kg of maize meal from Wholesaler B at the end of January 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 2020 price = $R659,70$ (RT - reading from table)
Mark 2: 2021 price = $R659,70 \times 105,17\%$ (multiplying by 105,17%)
Mark 3: $= R693,80649$ (simplification)
Mark 4: 2022 price = $R693,80649 \times 105,3\%$ (increasing with 5,3%)
Mark 5: $= R730,57823... \approx R730,58$ (simplification)

Alternatively: $R659,70 \times 1,0517 \times 1,053 = R730,58$

subQuestions.label: 1.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: A cylindrical 400 g can of fish has a label with diameter 73 mm and height 10,6 cm. Calculate (in cm²) the surface area of the label around the can. Use: Circumference of a circle = diameter × 3,142; Surface area of label around can = circumference × height.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Outer diameter = $73$ mm $= 7,3$ cm (conversion)
Mark 2: Circumference = $7,3 \times 3,142$ (substitution)
Mark 3: $= 22,9366$ cm (simplification)
Mark 4: Surface area = circumference × height = $22,9366 \times 10,6 = 243,12796$ cm² (simplification)

Alternative: Surface area = $7,3 \times 3,142 \times 10,6 = 243,12796$ cm²

subQuestions.label: 1.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the total length of a label if an overlap of 0,6 cm is needed for it to be glued around a can.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from 1.2.1(a)
Mark 1: Total length = circumference + overlap = $22,9366 \text{ cm} + 0,6 \text{ cm}$ (adding to circumference)
Mark 2: $= 23,5366$ cm (simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Some cans of fish are imported by ship, wrapped in packs of 12. Dimensions of a pack of 12 cans: Length 29,2 cm, Width 21,9 cm, Height 10,8 cm. The mass of an empty can is 40 g. The mass of a fully packed shipping crate with cans of fish is 280 kg. The inner dimensions of a shipping crate are 117 cm by 66 cm by 50 cm. Packs of cans are placed lengthwise (length to length) in the shipping crates. Aggie stated that an empty shipping crate has a mass of less than 20 kg. Verify, with calculations, if her statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Number of packs lengthwise = $\frac{117}{29,2} \approx 4$ (dividing 29,2)
Mark 2: Round down (R)
Mark 3: Number of packs width-wise = $\frac{66}{21,9} \approx 3$ (simplification)
Mark 4: Number of layers height-wise = $\frac{50}{10,8} = 4,63 \approx 4$ (simplification)
Mark 5: First layer has $4 \times 3 = 12$ packs; cans in a pack = $12 \times 12 = 144$ cans (simplification)
Mark 6: Number of cans in a crate = $144 \times 4 = 576$ (number of cans)
Mark 7: Mass = $576 \times 440 \text{ g} = 253\,440 \text{ g} = 253,44$ kg (mass of shipment, fish 400 g + can 40 g)
Mark 8: Mass of crate = $280 \text{ kg} - 253,44 \text{ kg} = 26,56$ kg (crate mass)
Mark 9: NOT VALID - the empty crate has mass 26,56 kg which is more than 20 kg (conclusion)

subQuestions.questionText: Tumi received a bursary to study at the University of Victoria in Canada. ANNEXURE A shows the map and two routes she could have used. In which general direction did she head from Cedar Hill Cross Road towards Crestview? (Refer to ANNEXURE A in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Marks 1-2: South East or SE (correct direction, 2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The total route via Cadboro Road and Pandora Avenue was 12 min (6,8 km). Sections: A1 Cedar Hill Cross Road (190 m), A2 Cadboro Road (3,2 km), A3 Fort Street (… km), A4 Pandora Avenue (2,1 km). Determine the distance that she travelled on Fort Street.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: All correct values (RT)
Mark 2: Distance = $6,8 \text{ km} - (0,19 + 3,2 + 2,1) \text{ km}$ (subtracting from 6,8 km)
Mark 3: $= 1,31$ km (simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the road she travelled on after crossing Flower Street. (Refer to ANNEXURE A in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Marks 1-2: Fort Street (correct street, 2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate (in km/h) the average speed she travelled. You may use the formula: Distance = Speed × Time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $12 \text{ min} = \frac{12}{60}$ hour $= 0,2$ hour (convert min to hour)
Mark 2: $6,8 \text{ km} = \text{speed} \times 12 \text{ min}$ (substitution)
Mark 3: Speed = $\frac{6,8 \text{ km}}{0,2 \text{ hour}}$ (changing subject of formula)
Mark 4: $= 34$ km/h (simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: On another day, Tumi travelled from the University of Victoria to Victoria Downtown via Shelburne at an average speed of 36,5 km/h. Calculate (in metres) the difference between the distances of the two routes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Distance = Speed × Time = $36,5 \text{ km/h} \times \frac{11}{60}$ h (correct values)
Mark 2: $= 6,69166667$ km (distance)
Mark 3: Difference = $6,8 \text{ km} - 6,69 \text{ km} = 0,1083333$ km $\approx 108,3$ m (simplification)
NPR if answer is in metres

subQuestions.questionText: Tumi rented a 1 045 square feet apartment. The balcony has dimensions 26 feet 10 inches by 4 feet, with stated area 109 sq.ft. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether the balcony with dimensions 26 feet 10 inches by 4 feet is greater or less than 109 square feet. You may use: Area of a rectangle = length × width. (1 foot = 12 inches; 1 inch = 25,4 mm)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Length = $(26 + \frac{10}{12})$ feet (adding)
Mark 2: Conversion of inches to feet
Mark 3: $= 26,83333...$ feet (simplification)
Mark 4: Area = $26,8333... \times 4$ feet (substitution)
Mark 5: $= 107,333...$ feet² (simplification)
Mark 6: Conclusion: LESS THAN 109 square feet

Alternative: $L = 26 \times 12 + 10 = 322$ inches; $W = 4 \times 12 = 48$ inches; Area = $322 \times 48 = 15\,456$ in² $= \frac{15\,456}{12^2} = 107,333$ feet² < 109 feet²

subQuestions.questionText: The southwest-facing wall, excluding the balcony, is 25 feet. Measure this distance on the layout plan to determine the scale in the form 1 cm : … feet.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Measured distance $= 82$ mm $= 8,2$ cm (measurement)
Mark 2: Scale: $8,2$ cm : $25$ feet, so $1$ cm : $\frac{25}{8,2}$ (scale)
Mark 3: $1$ cm : $3,05$ feet (simplification)
[Accept distances from 8 cm to 8,6 cm]

subQuestions.questionText: Tumi's monthly rent for her apartment is C$2 188,71 (C$ is Canadian dollar). Calculate the rental rate per square feet.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct values (RT): $\frac{2188,71}{1045}$
Mark 2: Dividing by 1 045 (M)
Mark 3: $= C\$2,09445... \approx C\$2,09$ per foot² (simplification)
NPR

subQuestions.questionText: A rental price ratio is used to calculate whether it is cheaper to rent or buy a property. Rental price ratio = Average property price / Average annual rent. Categories: Low (15 and below): better to buy; Moderate (15,1 to 20): usually better to rent; High (20,1 and above): definitely better to rent. The average house price is C$300 000 and the price to rent is C$6 000 per quarter. Advise Tumi, showing ALL calculations, whether she should rent or buy a property.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Annual rent $= C\$6\,000 \times 4 = C\$24\,000$ (calculating annual rent)
Mark 2: Price to rent ratio = $\frac{C\$300\,000}{C\$24\,000}$ (substitution)
Mark 3: $= 12,5$ (simplification)
Mark 4: Conclusion: Tumi should BUY (since 12,5 falls in the Low category, 15 and below)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: South Asian rental price ratios: 16,68; 12,00; 42,80; 12,55; 7,00; 10,82; 8,55; 13,56; 7,07; 29,86; 27,71; 6,84. Determine, in simplified fractional form, the probability of randomly selecting a South Asian city classified as high.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Numerator: 3 (cities classified as high - those with ratio 20,1 and above: 42,80; 29,86; 27,71)
Mark 2: Denominator: 12 (total number of South Asian cities)
Mark 3: $P = \frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}$ (simplification)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: The rental price ratios of selected cities in Africa are illustrated in a box and whisker plot with values: minimum 2,36; Q₁ unknown; median 12,19; Q₃ 17,89; maximum 27,41. Determine the value of Q₁ (the 1st quartile) if the interquartile range (IQR) for Africa is 14,25.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$ (IQR formula)
Mark 2: $14,25 = 17,89 - Q_1$ (substitution)
Mark 3: $Q_1 = 17,89 - 14,25 = 3,64$ (simplification)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Comment on the possibility of owning a property in these areas by comparing the minimum, maximum and median values for North America and Africa. (North American ratios: 2,11; 3,62; 4,24; 4,24; 4,68; 5,62; 5,87; 6,44; 6,52; 7,20; 7,59; 7,64; 7,64; 7,69; 8,32; 8,41; 8,72; 9,11; 11,08; 13,85; 15,26)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Minimum: North America (2,11) is lower than Africa (2,36)
Mark 2: Maximum: North America (15,26) is lower than Africa (27,41)
Mark 3: Median of North America = 7,59
Mark 4: Median: North America (7,59) is lower than Africa (12,19)
Mark 5: Conclusion: It is better to own/buy a house in North America

Summary table:
| | North America | Africa |
|---|---|---|
| Min | 2,11 | 2,36 |
| Max | 15,26 | 27,41 |
| Median | 7,59 | 12,19 |

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 2 shows data for South African assessed taxpayers for the 2018 tax year. Taxable income amounts (R million): Less than R1: -16 302; R1 to R70 000: 15 030; R70 001 to R350 000: 577 196; R350 001 to R500 000: 297 012; More than R500 000: 783 526; Total: C. Calculate missing value C.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $C = -16\,302 + 15\,030 + 577\,196 + 297\,012 + 783\,526$ (adding all correct values)
Mark 2: $= 1\,656\,462$ (simplification, AO)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine, to THREE decimal places, the probability of randomly choosing an assessed taxpayer if South Africa's population was 57,73 million in 2018. (Total assessed taxpayers = 4 917 029)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $57,730$ million $= 57\,730\,000$ (converting to number)
Mark 2: Numerator: $4\,917\,029$ (RT)
Mark 3: Denominator: $57\,730\,000$ (CA denominator)
Mark 4: $P = \frac{4\,917\,029}{57\,730\,000} \approx 0,085$ (simplification)

Alternative: $P = \frac{4,917029}{57,73} \approx 0,085$
P for rounding

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in rand, the mean monthly taxable income per taxpayer in the R70 001 to R350 000 taxable income group. (Number of taxpayers in this group: 2 856 043; Taxable income: R577 196 million)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct values (RT): R577 196 million; 2 856 043
Mark 2: Conversion: $R577\,196\,000\,000$ (conversion)
Mark 3: Mean = $\frac{577\,196\,000\,000}{2\,856\,043} = R202\,096,397$ (dividing by 2 856 043)
Mark 4: Monthly mean = $\frac{202\,096,397}{12}$ (dividing by 12)
Mark 5: $\approx R16\,841,37$ (simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: In the table, the percentage for tax assessed is 0,0% for the taxable income group R1 to R70 000. Explain, showing calculations, how this percentage was obtained. (Tax assessed for this group: R16 million; Total tax assessed: R356 199 million)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct values (RT): R16 million / R356 199 million
Mark 2: Percentage assessed = $\frac{16 \text{ million}}{356\,199 \text{ million}} \times 100\%$ (percentage calculation)
Mark 3: $= 0,00449\%$ (simplification)
Mark 4: Explanation: Rounded to 1 decimal place, this becomes 0,0% (explanation)

subQuestions.questionText: Emily earns a monthly gross salary of R26 904,22. She pays 7,5% of her gross salary towards her pension fund. In South Africa, taxable income is gross income minus payments towards a pension fund. Calculate Emily's annual taxable income.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Subtracting 7,5%: Monthly taxable income = $R26\,904,22 \times \frac{100-7,5}{100}$ (subtracting 7,5%)
Mark 2: $= R26\,904,22 \times 92,5\%$ (calculating %)
Mark 3: $= R24\,886,40$ (simplification)
Mark 4: Annual taxable income = $R24\,886,40 \times 12 = R298\,636,80$ (simplification)

subQuestions.questionText: The VAT rate in March 2018 was 14%. This rate was increased to 15% in April 2018. Emily bought an item, including VAT, for R172,50 in April 2018. Calculate the March 2018 price of this item, including VAT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: April price without VAT = $\frac{R172,50}{1,15}$ (dividing by 115%)
Mark 2: $= R150$ (simplification)
Mark 3: VAT in March = $R150 \times 14\% = R21$ (14% VAT)
Mark 4: March price with VAT = $R150 + R21 = R171$ (simplification)

Alternative: March Price = $\frac{R172,50}{1,15} \times 1,14 = R171$

subQuestions.label: 3.2.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: ANNEXURE B shows the distribution of assessed taxpayers and income tax per province represented by arrows. Arrange the provinces in descending order of tax assessed. (Refer to ANNEXURE B in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks 1-2: All correct provinces (RT, 2 marks)
Marks 3-4: Correct order (A, 2 marks)

Descending order: Gauteng, Western Cape, KZN, Eastern Cape, Mpumalanga, Limpopo, North West, Free State, Northern Cape

subQuestions.label: 3.2.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason why all these arrows have different lengths.
subQuestions.memoText: Marks 1-2: It is to show that all provinces are different (taxpayers' population/filers and tax due to income), OR Tax collected per province differ due to a number of factors (e.g. taxpayers and percentage, tax assessed and percentage, taxpayers' salary). (2 marks reason)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.3(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Emily stated that when comparing the lengths of the arrows of the North West and Free State, they varied proportionally according to the tax-assessed percentage. Verify whether her statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: NOT VALID (1 mark)
Marks 2-3: Reason: percentage of North West is higher than that of Free State but the arrow is shorter, OR Free State tax assessed and percentage is lower than that of the North West, however the Free State arrow is taller, OR the arrow lengths vary according to the number of taxpayers (2 marks reason)

subQuestions.questionText: The South African taxi association published its results for the year ended September 2019: 250 000 minibus taxis are currently doing business in South Africa; the net worth of the minibus taxi industry is R50 billion a year; minibus taxis are responsible for 15 million commuter trips daily; minibus taxis travel 19 billion kilometres a year. It is given that there is one bus for every 13,2 minibus taxis on the road. Determine, to the nearest thousand, the number of buses needed to replace the minibus taxis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Number of buses = $\frac{250\,000}{13,2}$ (dividing by 13,2)
Mark 2: $= 18\,939,39394$ (simplification)
Mark 3: $\approx 19\,000$ (rounding to nearest thousand)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Two exchange rates: A: 1 euro = 15,97 ZAR; B: 1 euro = 15,966728 ZAR. Calculate (in euros) the difference in net worth of the minibus taxi industry using exchange rates A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Exchange rate A: $\frac{R50\,000\,000\,000}{R15,97}$ (dividing by exchange rate)
Mark 2: $= 3\,130\,870\,382$ euros (simplification)
Mark 3: Exchange rate B: $\frac{R50\,000\,000\,000}{R15,966728}$ (dividing by exchange rate)
Mark 4: $= 3\,131\,511\,979$ euros (simplification)
Mark 5: Difference = $(3\,131\,511\,979 - 3\,130\,870\,382)$ euros (subtracting)
Mark 6: $= €641\,597$ (simplification)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Justify which exchange rate (A or B) they should use when doing the presentation to their European clients.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from 4.1.2(a)
Mark 1: Choice: Exchange rate B
Marks 2-3: Reason: It gives a higher value (€641 597 more), shows more money will be made for the taxis, OR it is stronger against the Euro (2 marks reason)

subQuestions.questionText: The ratio of the number of daily commuter trips is given as: train : bus : minibus taxi is 4 : 5 : 75. Calculate the number of commuters who do NOT use a minibus taxi daily. (Total daily trips by minibus taxi = 15 million)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Total parts = $4 + 5 + 75 = 84$ (simplification)
Mark 2: $\frac{75}{84} \times \text{total commuters} = 15\,000\,000$ (working with ratio)
Mark 3: Total commuters = $\frac{15\,000\,000 \times 84}{75} = 16\,800\,000$ (simplification)
Mark 4: Number not using a taxi = $16\,800\,000 - 15\,000\,000 = 1\,800\,000$ (simplification)

Alternative: Not using taxi = $4 + 5 = 9$; $\frac{15\,000\,000}{75} \times 9 = 1\,800\,000$

subQuestions.questionText: The average distance between the moon and Earth is 384 402 km. A minibus taxi owner stated that the distance travelled by minibus taxis in one year is more than 24 000 trips to the moon and back. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether the statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Distance to moon and back = $384\,402 \times 2$ (multiplying by 2)
Mark 2: $= 768\,804$ km (simplification)
Mark 3: Number of trips = $\frac{19\,000\,000\,000}{768\,804}$ (dividing)
Mark 4: $= 24\,713,71117$ (simplification)
Mark 5: VALID, more than 24 000 (conclusion)

subQuestions.questionText: Transaction Capital is listed on the JSE. ANNEXURE C shows the share price of Transaction Capital for the period 9 January 2015 to 3 January 2020. Write down the total number of days covered by the period shown in ANNEXURE C. (Refer to ANNEXURE C in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Number of days in full year (e.g., 9 Jan 2015 to 9 Jan 2016 = 365 days)
Mark 2: Days till 3 Jan (9 Jan 2019 to 3 Jan 2020 = 359 days)
Mark 3: Adding (MCA)
Mark 4: Total = $365 + 366 + 730 + 359 = 1\,820$ days (simplification)

Alternative: $365 \times 5 + 1 - 6 = 1\,820$ days

subQuestions.questionText: Determine (in cents) the value of a share on 9 January 2015 if it was R12,68 less than the amount shown on 3 January 2020. (Share price on 3 January 2020 = R20,63 = 2063c)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Share price in cents = $2063 - 1268$ (subtracting converted amount; R12,68 = 1268c)
Mark 2: $= 795$ cents (simplification)

subQuestions.label: 4.2.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Verify, showing calculations, whether the following statement is CORRECT: Transaction Capital's share price went down by 3,51% for the day ending 3 January 2020. (Previous day price was 2138c, current is 2063c)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct values (RT): 2063 and 2138
Mark 2: Substitution into % change formula: $\frac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100\%$
Mark 3: % change calculation: $\frac{2063 - 2138}{2138} \times 100\%$
Mark 4: $= -3,50795\%$ (simplification)
Mark 5: CORRECT - it went down by 3,51% rounded to 2 decimal places (conclusion)

subQuestions.label: 4.2.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Verify, showing calculations, whether the following statement is CORRECT: At the beginning of each year 80% of the time, share prices went down.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reasoning - share prices went down in 4 years: 2016, 2017, 2019, and 2020 (went up in 2018)
Mark 2: Verification of percentage: $\frac{4}{5} \times 100\% = 80\%$
Mark 3: Conclusion: Statement is CORRECT

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate (in rand) the profit a person will make if he/she bought 5 000 shares at the 52-week lowest price and sold them when the price was at its highest. (52-week low = 1611c; 52-week high = 2350c)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct values (RT): 1611c and 2350c
Mark 2: Buying = $5\,000 \times 1\,611 = 8\,055\,000$c (buy)
Mark 3: Converting to rand: $= R80\,550$ (conversion)
Mark 4: Sell = $5\,000 \times 2\,350 = 11\,750\,000$c $= R117\,500$ (CA sell)
Mark 5: Profit = $R117\,500 - R80\,550 = R36\,950$ (simplification)

Alternative: Difference in price = $2\,350 - 1\,611 = 739$c $= R7,39$; Profit = $R7,39 \times 5\,000 = R36\,950$
